title: Pythagoras' theorem: finding the third side

slides.title: Finding the third side of a triangle
slides.prompt: A ladder leaning on a wall, a diagonal across a rectangle, the height of a roof. All of them are right-angled triangles. If you know two sides of a right-angled triangle, one rule gives you the third. By the end of this lesson you will have written 18 marks of real exam answers, including one from a past paper.

slides.title: The rule
slides.prompt: Count the areas. The blue square is $16$, the orange square is $9$, and the pink square on the longest side is exactly $25$. So $16 + 9 = 25$. In any right-angled triangle, $a^2 + b^2 = c^2$. The letter $c$ is always the side opposite the right angle.

slides.title: The steps for every question
slides.prompt: Every Pythagoras question uses the same five steps. Circling the two things first is what tells you whether to add or subtract.

visual.content:
1Circle what you are given.
2Circle what you need to find.
3Find the hypotenuse. It is the side opposite the right angle.
4If you need the hypotenuse, add the squares. If not, subtract.
5Take the square root at the end.
